title: Projectile speed as the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity vector

authority_basis.claim_scope: Repository-backed SBA04 atom builds speed from vx and vy, distinguishes speed from signed components and identifies apex minimum speed.

concepts.statement: Projectile speed is the nonnegative magnitude of the instantaneous velocity vector reconstructed from its signed components.
concepts.why_required: Speed must be separated from velocity direction and component signs.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Negative vy may be misread as negative speed or one component may be used as the whole speed.

concepts.statement: In the standard oblique projectile model with constant horizontal velocity, speed is minimized when the vertical component passes through zero at the apex.
concepts.why_required: The apex minimum follows from vector magnitude, not from the projectile stopping.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Minimum speed may be incorrectly set to zero or placed at another event.

conditions: Components refer to the same velocity state

model_conditions.condition: Velocity components are orthogonal components of the same state, with vx constant in the standard no-drag projectile model when using the apex-minimum claim.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The magnitude relation is geometric, while the minimum-at-apex result additionally depends on constant vx and vy passing through zero.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: With drag or propulsion, speed extrema need not occur at the standard apex event.

representations.semantic_geometry: Signed vx and vy components form a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the nonnegative speed magnitude; apex comparison removes the vertical leg but retains vx.
must_not_imply: one component alone is always the speed
representations.verification_method: Square and reconstruct the component magnitude, then set vy=0 at apex and confirm v=|vx| rather than zero.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Obtain signed current velocity components for one state.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Speed may be computed from stale or mismatched components.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Reconstruct the nonnegative magnitude using the component norm.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Component sign can be incorrectly carried into scalar speed.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: For the standard apex event set vy=0 while retaining vx to identify the minimum speed.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Minimum speed may be equated with zero total velocity.

required_transformations.description: Translate signed velocity components into scalar speed while preserving the distinction between magnitude and direction.
Use the component-magnitude relation with the apex event condition to solve minimum-speed or inverse component questions and independently verify the nonzero horizontal contribution.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The projectile's speed is zero at the apex because vertical velocity is zero.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The vertical component changes sign there and is often emphasized as zero.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: For an oblique launch with nonzero ux, the projectile crosses the apex horizontally with speed |ux|.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the apex speed triangle collapsed to the horizontal leg rather than to a point.
misconceptions.verification: Substitute vy=0 into the speed-magnitude relation.

problem_families.name: Projectile speed magnitude and apex minimum
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the current components and form v^2=vx^2+vy^2 before applying event conditions.
